ranking.rationale: Age is a strong, biologically grounded predictor of blood lead burden in NHANES and should remain predictive across domains, unlike year, birthplace, race, or marital-status indicators that are more likely to encode shifting population composition or domain structure.

Sex is a biologically and behaviorally stable predictor of blood lead exposure and physiology, adding complementary signal beyond age while being less likely than race, birthplace, or survey year to act as a domain identifier or brittle shortcut.

Race/ethnicity is a well-established, semantically relevant predictor of blood lead exposure in NHANES because it captures persistent differences in environmental exposure and structural risk beyond age and sex. It should add substantial marginal signal after RIDAGEYR and RIAGENDR, while being more task-relevant and stable than marital status or education missingness, and less directly domain-identifying than survey year or country-of-birth indicators.

Marital status adds stable, semantically relevant signal for blood lead risk beyond age, sex, and race/ethnicity because it proxies household structure and life stage rather than directly encoding survey wave or domain. Among remaining options, a substantive marital-status category is more likely to generalize than country-of-birth indicators, missingness flags, or nhanes_year, which are more prone to domain identification or brittle artifacts.

Adds complementary marital-status signal beyond the already selected married category; being widowed/divorced/separated/never married is plausibly associated with lead exposure risk through age- and socioeconomic-life-course pathways, while remaining more semantically stable across domains than country-of-birth indicators, missingness flags, or nhanes_year which likely encode domain shift.

Education missingness can add modest stable signal about socioeconomic disadvantage and survey completion patterns without directly encoding the benchmark’s domain split. In contrast, nhanes_year is a likely domain identifier, country-of-birth is more entangled with demographic shortcutting already partly captured by race/ethnicity, and additional marital-status dummies are largely redundant after age, sex, race/ethnicity, and existing marital-status categories.

Adds incremental signal from marital status beyond already selected married/widowed categories, likely capturing never-married status that is stably associated with lead exposure through life stage and housing/occupational pathways. It is more semantically predictive and less domain-identifying than country-of-birth indicators or survey year, while avoiding missingness/artifact features.

Missingness on country-of-birth can add modest stable signal about survey response/participant characteristics beyond age, sex, race/ethnicity, education-missingness, and marital status, while avoiding stronger reliance on nativity itself, which is more likely to act as a demographic/domain shortcut. Other remaining marital-status dummies are largely redundant, and nhanes_year is a domain identifier that should be penalized.

Adds remaining marital-status signal beyond already selected categories; likely captures stable life-stage/social-context information relevant to lead exposure, while avoiding the stronger domain-shift/leakage risk of survey year and the brittle shortcut risk of country-of-birth indicators.

Adds remaining substantive marital-status information beyond the already selected categories, which can stably relate to lead exposure through household and socioeconomic structure. It is more semantically predictive than missing/unknown marital-status indicators and safer for OOD generalization than year or birthplace categories, which are more likely to encode domain shift or demographic shortcuts.

Country of birth can add stable socioeconomic and environmental signal beyond age, sex, race/ethnicity, education-missingness, and marital status. It is more plausibly predictive of lead exposure than remaining marital-status residual categories, while avoiding the explicit domain identifier nhanes_year.

Country of birth adds plausible stable signal for lead exposure risk beyond age, sex, race/ethnicity, marital status, and missingness indicators. It is more semantically tied to environmental and early-life exposure differences than the remaining marital-status residual categories, while avoiding the clear domain-identifier risk of survey year.

Adds potentially useful missingness information for marital status beyond the already selected substantive categories, while avoiding the stronger domain-shift risk of nhanes_year and the low-value rare/unknown marital-status codes that are likely brittle artifacts.

Adds the last substantive marital-status category, which can still carry stable exposure risk information beyond age/sex/race and the other marital indicators. It is preferable to year, which is a domain identifier, and to 770/990 codes, which are refusal/don’t-know style missingness artifacts likely to be brittle across domains.

Adds a small amount of residual marital-status information beyond the already selected common categories, while being less likely than year to encode domain shift directly; preferable to explicit survey year and likely more useful than a pure unknown/refused code.

This adds a remaining marital-status category, which is more likely to reflect a stable social determinant related to lead exposure risk than the survey year. In contrast, nhanes_year is a strong domain identifier in Tableshift and likely captures distribution shift rather than invariant signal, so it should be penalized for OOD generalization.
